main.title: Murdered: Soul Suspect
main.subtitle: Investigate your own murder as a ghost in Salem
main.summary: Murdered: Soul Suspect is a 2014 action-adventure stealth video game developed by Airtight Games and Square Enix. The game was released in June 2014 for PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Windows, Xbox 360, and Xbox One. The game is played in a third-person view as the player navigates the protagonist, detective Ronan O'Connor, around a fictionalized version of Salem, Massachusetts. The story centers on Ronan as he hunts down an infamous serial killer known as the Bell Killer. After being killed by the Bell Killer at the beginning of the game, Ronan returns as a ghost. He is then informed by his long-dead wife, Julia, that he must solve the Bell Killer mystery so he can rejoin her.

cards.heading: A murdered detective returns as a ghost
cards.text: Murdered: Soul Suspect is a 2014 supernatural investigation game from Airtight Games and Square Enix, released for PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Windows, Xbox 360 and Xbox One. Detective Ronan O'Connor is killed by Salem's Bell Killer and returns as a ghost. His dead wife, Julia, tells him that solving the mystery will allow them to be reunited. The case therefore begins with the detective investigating the crime that ended his own life.

cards.heading: Search Salem for clues with supernatural abilities
cards.text: Ronan searches a fictionalised Salem, including an apartment building, a church and a graveyard. Collecting clues advances the investigation, while possession and teleportation give him supernatural ways to approach the places he visits. The investigation sequences draw a comparison with L.A. Noire, but Ronan's ghostly condition provides their particular setting. Collectible papers and Ghost Girl Messages offer further information alongside the main case, including details about Ronan's life.

cards.heading: The question that inspired a ghost detective
cards.text: The premise began with Square Enix creative director Yosuke Shiokawa considering how an action hero might continue trying to save people after being killed. Die Hard supplied his example: he imagined John McClane carrying on as a ghost. He brought the idea to Airtight Games, whose team explored several directions before developing the murdered detective. That starting question linked a familiar kind of investigation to a protagonist whose death was the beginning of the story.

main.title: Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth
main.subtitle: Two casts meet inside a labyrinth
main.summary: Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth is Atlus' Nintendo 3DS dungeon role-playing crossover bringing together the casts of Persona 3 and Persona 4. They find themselves in an unfamiliar version of Yasogami High School with Zen and Rei, two young people who have lost their memories. Escaping requires exploring the labyrinths connected to the school and recovering objects hidden within them. The familiar characters provide the conversations and party choices, while the first-person exploration draws on the map-making approach of Atlus' Etrian Odyssey series.

They find themselves in an unfamiliar version of Yasogami High School with Zen and Rei, two young people who have lost their memories. cards.heading: Draw the route while following it
cards.text: The upper screen presents corridors from the party's viewpoint, while the touchscreen holds a map that the player develops during exploration. Marking walls, passages and useful features turns progress through a maze into a record that can be consulted on the next visit. Battles use turn-based decisions and the abilities associated with Personas. Choosing a party therefore affects both its practical options and the characters sharing the expedition. Learning a dungeon means understanding its layout as well as preparing a group capable of surviving the encounters along the route.

cards.heading: The school becomes a base
cards.text: Between expeditions, the school provides places to recover, sell collected materials, obtain equipment and work with Personas. These services connect discoveries inside the labyrinths with preparation for the next attempt. The crossover also creates space for conversations between characters who originally belonged to separate adventures. Their relationships develop around a shared immediate problem, rather than requiring the player to repeat the original stories. A return to the school offers a pause, a chance to adjust the team and another reason to take the assembled cast back into the maze.

main.title: Valiant Hearts: The Great War
main.subtitle: Follow four lives and a faithful dog through the Great War
main.summary: Valiant Hearts: The Great War is a 2014 puzzle adventure game developed by Ubisoft Montpellier and published by Ubisoft.

cards.heading: Four lives in the Great War
cards.text: Valiant Hearts: The Great War is a 2014 puzzle adventure game developed by Ubisoft Montpellier and published by Ubisoft. The game was released for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Xbox 360, and Xbox One in June 2014. Set during World War I, the game follows four characters who help a young German soldier find his love in a story about survival, sacrifice, and friendship. Players solve puzzles by interacting with various objects and people. The characters are accompanied by a dog named Walt who helps players solve puzzles. Collectible items hidden in each chapter reveal facts about the war.

cards.heading: Puzzles and the tools of survival
cards.text: The game comprises four chapters split into several sections. Each section requires the player to clear an objective to progress through the story. Most of these involve solving puzzles by obtaining certain items needed for the situation. Other sections include wartime segments requiring the player to survive heavy gunfire, stealth sections where the player must avoid being detected by enemies, and rhythmic car chase sections set to classic songs. Each character can interact with objects, perform a melee attack to knock out guards or smash through debris, and throw projectiles. There are also some traits unique to each character. Emile has a shovel which lets him dig through soft ground, Freddie can cut through barbed wire, and Anna can treat patients for injuries, which requires the player to time button presses.

cards.heading: Walt and the hidden histories
cards.text: Players can issue various commands to a dog named Walt, who is able to squeeze into small areas, hold on to and fetch certain items, activate switches, and move around without being suspected by the enemy. The game features optional collectible items hidden in each segment, facts about the war that are unlocked as the game progresses, and a hint system the player can use if they are stuck on a section after a certain amount of time.

cards.heading: Remembering the war through UbiArt
cards.text: Ubisoft Montpellier developed Valiant Hearts for the centenary of World War I in 2014. The story follows people on both sides of the conflict through the difficulties of survival and separation. The team read soldiers' letters, listened to first-hand accounts and visited the remains of trenches in France. LucasArts adventures and The Cave provided references for its puzzles. The UbiArt Framework, previously used for Rayman Legends, supported the illustrated presentation.

cards.heading: Reception and a continuing story
cards.text: Upon release, The Great War received generally positive reviews. Critics praised the game's themes, visuals, animation, and music, and applauded the developer for enabling players to learn more about history while playing the game. However, reception to the game's story and gameplay was mixed. Valiant Hearts was nominated for several year-end awards, including Best Narrative at The Game Awards 2014. Ubisoft later released the game on additional platforms including iOS, Android, Nintendo Switch, and Google Stadia. A sequel, Valiant Hearts: Coming Home, was released in 2023 for Netflix Games and 2024 for Windows and home consoles.

main.title: Shovel Knight
main.subtitle: Explore a knight’s original quest with a shovel in hand
main.summary: Shovel Knight is a platform game developed and published by Yacht Club Games.

cards.heading: A crowdfunded adventure inspired by NES platformers
cards.text: Shovel Knight is Yacht Club Games' crowdfunded platform adventure, first released for Nintendo 3DS, Wii U and Windows in June 2014. Its armoured hero sets out to rescue Shield Knight from the Enchantress and the Order of No Quarter. His shovel serves as a weapon, a digging tool and a way to bounce from enemies and objects. The eight-bit presentation draws on NES games, while each knight's themed stage leads towards a boss fight.

cards.heading: Treasure, checkpoints and a growing adventure
cards.text: Collected treasure buys upgrades and magical Relics, including a fireball wand and a locket that grants temporary invulnerability. Dying leaves some gold behind, recoverable until the next death. Players can also destroy checkpoints for treasure, accepting a longer return after a mistake. Later campaigns expanded the game around other characters. The original quest became Shovel of Hope, and the 2019 Treasure Trove collection brought it together with Plague of Shadows, Specter of Torment, King of Cards and the multiplayer fighting game Showdown.

cards.heading: Spin-offs and a planned remake
cards.text: A spin-off dungeon crawler puzzle game, Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon, was co-developed with Vine and released on December 13, 2021, for macOS, Windows, Nintendo Switch, and PlayStation 4. A prequel, the roguelike Shovel Knight Dig, was co-developed with Nitrome and released on September 23, 2022, for Windows, Nintendo Switch, and Apple Arcade. A remake of the first game called Shovel of Hope DX is planned to be released at a future date.

main.title: Divinity: Original Sin
main.subtitle: Discover Larian’s original role-playing adventure and its creation tools
main.summary: Divinity: Original Sin is a role-playing video game developed and published by Larian Studios.

cards.heading: An original adventure before Divine Divinity
cards.text: Divinity: Original Sin is Larian Studios' role-playing adventure, first released for Windows in June 2014. Set before Divine Divinity, it follows two Source Hunters sent to investigate a councillor's murder in the port of Cyseal. One player can control both protagonists, or two players can take a hunter each in cooperative play. Their investigation opens onto a wider conflict in Rivellon, with turn-based battles forming part of the journey.

cards.heading: Crowdfunding, the editor and the later Enhanced Edition
cards.text: Part of the project's funding came from Kickstarter, while the finished game included the editor used to build it. Players could create single-player or multiplayer adventures and publish them online, extending the tools of the original campaign to their own scenarios. The 2015 Enhanced Edition expanded the story and gameplay options and brought the adventure to additional platforms. A sequel followed in 2017.

main.title: Yo-kai Watch 2
main.subtitle: A familiar town gains another history
main.summary: Yo-kai Watch 2 is Level-5's Nintendo 3DS role-playing sequel, first released in Japan as two versions later known as Bony Spirits and Fleshy Souls. Nate or Katie must recover a connection with the Yo-kai after losing both the watch and the memories associated with it. The adventure expands the places and creatures surrounding Springdale, with an enlarged roster and another journey behind its everyday troubles. Psychic Specters subsequently extended the same adventure, adding further material to the conflict introduced by the original pair of versions.

cards.heading: A familiar town gains another history
cards.text: Yo-kai Watch 2 is Level-5's Nintendo 3DS role-playing sequel, first released in Japan as two versions later known as Bony Spirits and Fleshy Souls. Nate or Katie must recover a connection with the Yo-kai after losing both the watch and the memories associated with it. The adventure expands the places and creatures surrounding Springdale, with an enlarged roster and another journey behind its everyday troubles. Psychic Specters subsequently extended the same adventure, adding further material to the conflict introduced by the original pair of versions.

cards.heading: A stronger move has a price
cards.text: Battles retain the six-member medal wheel and three active Yo-kai, allowing the player to rotate companions into the fight. The newer watch introduces G Soultimates, stronger special moves that draw on the soul meters of neighbouring team members. Using one therefore involves the readiness of more than a single creature. Touchscreen interactions continue to support the automatically acting party. The familiar arrangement gains another decision about when to spend a shared resource, especially when a powerful response now could leave nearby companions less prepared for what comes next.

cards.heading: Find the right moment to make a friend
cards.text: Befriending Yo-kai still involves encountering them and offering suitable food. A new poking interaction allows the player to search for a useful spot on an enemy, producing benefits that can include improved friendship chances or additional rewards. This gives the touchscreen another task during an encounter rather than leaving all attention on the medal wheel. The larger roster makes those individual meetings part of a longer collection. Returning creatures provide continuity, while new forms of interaction give the player more ways to influence how a meeting ends.

main.title: Oreshika: Tainted Bloodlines
main.subtitle: The party is a family that cannot live long
main.summary: Oreshika: Tainted Bloodlines is Alfa System's PlayStation Vita role-playing game, first released in Japan on 17 July 2014. A cursed family confronts demons while its members are limited to very short lives, making descendants essential to the campaign. The player develops a lineage rather than expecting one unchanged party to reach the end. Children inherit traits from their parents and continue the work after them. The structure makes time part of character development: a strong fighter is valuable now, but the future of the family depends on what can be passed on before that life ends.

cards.text: Oreshika: Tainted Bloodlines is Alfa System's PlayStation Vita role-playing game, first released in Japan on 17 July 2014. A cursed family confronts demons while its members are limited to very short lives, making descendants essential to the campaign. The player develops a lineage rather than expecting one unchanged party to reach the end. Children inherit traits from their parents and continue the work after them. The structure makes time part of character development: a strong fighter is valuable now, but the future of the family depends on what can be passed on before that life ends.

cards.heading: Prepare the next generation while fighting the present battle
cards.text: Victories provide the means to form unions with deities and bring new children into the family. The player chooses names and classes, developing a group whose abilities must serve both the next expedition and the longer lineage. Dungeon encounters supply experience, equipment and techniques, while the mansion provides a central place to manage the family. A character's limited lifespan changes the meaning of investment. Training is still useful, but it belongs to an ongoing household whose strength must survive the departure of the particular person carrying it.

cards.heading: A Japanese visual tradition shapes the family
cards.text: Shoji Masuda directed and designed the game, with Konosuke Kihara composing its music. The style draws on traditional Japanese artwork while three-dimensional faces make inherited resemblances visible. It follows an earlier PlayStation game without requiring direct knowledge of that story, placing the new family a century later. North American and European digital releases followed in March 2015. The campaign's distinctive achievement is to make succession playable, connecting the emotional loss of a developed character to the practical arrival of someone whose appearance and capabilities preserve part of the person who came before.

main.title: P.T.
main.subtitle: The same corridor becomes less familiar each time
main.summary: P.T. is Kojima Productions' PlayStation 4 psychological-horror teaser, released on 12 August 2014. An unknown person walks through a domestic corridor that leads back to its own beginning, with each repetition introducing changes that are difficult to anticipate. The player's actions are limited to moving and looking more closely, making attention itself the main means of progress. A small house becomes threatening through repetition rather than scale. The player learns its shape quickly, then loses confidence in what that knowledge can guarantee when the next loop begins.

cards.heading: The same corridor becomes less familiar each time
cards.text: P.T. is Kojima Productions' PlayStation 4 psychological-horror teaser, released on 12 August 2014. An unknown person walks through a domestic corridor that leads back to its own beginning, with each repetition introducing changes that are difficult to anticipate. The player's actions are limited to moving and looking more closely, making attention itself the main means of progress. A small house becomes threatening through repetition rather than scale. The player learns its shape quickly, then loses confidence in what that knowledge can guarantee when the next loop begins.

cards.heading: Look again at the place you thought you knew
cards.text: The bathroom, corridor and returning staircase supply a compact set of spaces in which sounds and small visual differences become important. Cryptic requirements encourage investigation, while the presence of Lisa makes waiting and turning around feel dangerous. The player has few tools for resolving that uncertainty through force. Instead, progress depends on noticing a change and deciding whether approaching it is necessary. The limited layout gives each detail more weight: a light, doorway or noise can alter the meaning of the whole route because there is so little else competing for attention.

cards.heading: A teaser outlives the project it introduced
cards.text: Released under the name 7780s Studio, the teaser eventually revealed Silent Hills, a planned collaboration involving Hideo Kojima and Guillermo del Toro. Ludvig Forssell composed its music. Konami removed P.T. from the PlayStation Store after the larger game's cancellation, making an ordinary reinstall impossible. Its influence continued through other horror games and fan recreations. The release demonstrates how a brief interactive work can become memorable through precise limits, using one repeated domestic space to make the player increasingly uncertain about the next few steps rather than promising a larger world beyond them.

main.title: Hyrule Warriors
main.subtitle: Zelda characters fight across the large battlefields of a Musou game
main.summary: Zelda characters and weapons join the large battlefields, keeps and objectives of Dynasty Warriors.

cards.heading: Zelda enters the Musou battlefield
cards.text: Hyrule Warriors is Omega Force and Team Ninja's 2014 action game for Wii U, combining Zelda characters and equipment with the large battles of Dynasty Warriors. Link and other fighters move between keeps and shifting fronts, cutting through groups of enemies while responding to objectives elsewhere on the map. Choosing where to intervene becomes part of winning the battle.

cards.heading: Familiar weapons against armies of enemies
cards.text: Hyrule Warriors mixes the hack and slash gameplay of Koei Tecmo's Dynasty Warriors series of video games with settings and characters from Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda series. Amongst many other characters, the player controls an original iteration of Link in melee combat to take on large numbers of enemies from the Legend of Zelda series. While there is a much stronger emphasis on combat than other games in the Legend of Zelda series, the player may use common weapons from prior games in the series, such as a sword, bombs, and Link's signature spin attack. Enemy targeting also returns, in combination with elements from the Dynasty Warriors combat system. Obtaining items through discovering and opening chests is retained as well.

cards.heading: Weapons, character growth and local cooperation
cards.text: The game has a context-based combat system, in which the player character's abilities change depending on the weapon chosen. Role-playing elements such as weapons and character leveling also appear. Defeating certain enemies gives players weapon bags, which will grant a random weapon to the character, and materials bags, which can be used to power up characters. "Sealed weapons" may also be found in treasure boxes, which increase the types of weapons randomly generated for the player in the field. The game supports an asymmetric local two-player mode with one player using the Wii U GamePad and another using a monitor. The game is also compatible with Amiibo figures, with figures based on The Legend of Zelda series unlocking additional content such as new weapons.

cards.heading: Nintendo, Omega Force and Team Ninja collaborate
cards.text: Team Ninja's Yosuke Hayashi and Koei Tecmo's Hisashi Koinuma proposed the crossover, drawing on their enthusiasm for Zelda. Omega Force brought its experience with Dynasty Warriors, while Team Ninja contributed to one-on-one combat and other design ideas. Eiji Aonuma supervised the project for Nintendo, with Shigeru Miyamoto helping bring him into development. The collaboration was announced in a Nintendo Direct in December 2013, ahead of the Wii U release the following year.

main.title: inFAMOUS First Light
main.subtitle: Seattle seen through a neon trail
main.summary: inFAMOUS First Light is Sucker Punch Productions' PlayStation 4 action-adventure, released in North America on 26 August 2014. Abigail Walker, known as Fetch, recounts the events that brought her into custody at Curdun Cay. Her story precedes Second Son and gives one of its supporting characters an adventure of her own. Neon powers carry her across a fictional Seattle and shape the way she fights. The standalone release does not require Second Son, making its shorter campaign an independent way to enter this part of the setting.

cards.heading: Seattle seen through a neon trail
cards.text: inFAMOUS First Light is Sucker Punch Productions' PlayStation 4 action-adventure, released in North America on 26 August 2014. Abigail Walker, known as Fetch, recounts the events that brought her into custody at Curdun Cay. Her story precedes Second Son and gives one of its supporting characters an adventure of her own. Neon powers carry her across a fictional Seattle and shape the way she fights. The standalone release does not require Second Son, making its shorter campaign an independent way to enter this part of the setting.

cards.heading: Follow the light through the city
cards.text: Fetch can move at speed using her neon abilities, turning travel across streets and buildings into a flowing route toward the next objective. The same power supplies attacks whose precision and timing become important against groups of enemies. Sources of neon in the city connect movement and combat to the surroundings, giving the familiar urban map a different practical meaning from another character's route through it. Completing activities develops those abilities, making Fetch progressively more effective at linking an approach, a shot and an escape through the same space.

cards.heading: A story and a place to practise it
cards.text: The campaign alternates Fetch's memories with her imprisonment, while challenge arenas concentrate on fighting successive threats and improving a score. Those arenas give the powers room to be used without another story mission determining the pace. Nate Fox directed the project, supported by music from Marc Canham, Nathan Johnson and Brain. Critics generally welcomed Fetch's abilities and the presentation, with more mixed responses to the story's scale and combat. Its focused set of powers makes it a character study expressed through movement as well as the events Fetch describes.
